text: If the Moon disappeared tonight, the biggest change wouldn't be in the sky... it would be in the ocean.
The Moon's gravity pulls on our seas, creating the tides. Without it, the tides would shrink to about a third of their size.
Beaches and rock pools that depend on the tides would change forever, and lots of sea creatures living there would struggle.
Nights would get much darker too. No moonlight at all... just stars.
That's a big problem for animals. Corals use the full moon as a signal to release their eggs, all at the same time.
And you could say goodbye to total solar eclipses. There'd be nothing to block the Sun.
Even our calendars would feel strange. The word month actually comes from the word moon!
Over millions of years, Earth's tilt could start to wobble without the Moon to steady it, causing wild, extreme seasons.
But here's the crazy part. The Moon actually is leaving us, right now.
It drifts about four centimetres further away every year. That's roughly as fast as your fingernails grow.
Don't worry though. It'll be around for billions of years. So go and enjoy the view tonight.
